question: Where inside an atom do gamma rays come from?
explanation: Gamma rays are released from changes inside the nucleus of a radioactive atom. X-rays, by contrast, come from electrons outside the nucleus. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T5#BMP112_U6_T5_h1)

question: How are gamma rays different from sound waves?

options.A: Sound waves carry ionizing energy particles
options.B: Gamma rays can only move through solid objects
options.C: Gamma rays travel without needing a physical medium
options.D: Sound waves have a much higher frequency than gamma rays

explanation: Electromagnetic waves like gamma rays can travel through empty space. Sound waves require a solid, liquid, or gas medium to move. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T5#BMP112_U6_T5_h1)

question: What happens to an atom's nucleus when it gives off a gamma ray?

options.A: It drops from an excited state to a stable state
options.B: It gains an extra proton from the surrounding tissue
options.C: It loses two neutrons through nuclear fission
options.D: It converts completely into a different chemical element

explanation: Gamma emission rids the nucleus of excess energy without changing the number of protons or neutrons, leaving the element the same. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T5#BMP112_U6_T5_h2)

question: Which type of radioactive decay usually happens right before gamma rays are released?
explanation: Atomic nuclei often stay in an unstable, excited energy state right after ejecting alpha or beta particles, causing them to release gamma rays next. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T5#BMP112_U6_T5_h2)

question: What is the electric charge of a gamma photon?
explanation: Gamma rays are pure electromagnetic energy with no electrical charge, which means magnetic fields cannot bend or deflect them. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T5#BMP112_U6_T5_h3)

question: Why do gamma rays need dense materials like lead to block them?

options.A: They react instantly with air to create electrical sparks
options.B: They attract magnetic metals and destroy them on contact
options.C: They have high penetrating power and pass easily through light materials
options.D: They carry heavy physical mass that breaks down thin barriers

explanation: Because they lack mass and charge, gamma rays pass right through low-density matter. Very dense atoms packed closely together are needed to absorb them. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T5#BMP112_U6_T5_h3)

question: Why is a developing fetus especially sensitive to gamma radiation?

options.A: Fetal bone structures absorb all gamma rays like a sponge
options.B: Fetal tissues contain rapidly dividing cells that are easily damaged
options.C: Unborn babies lack any cellular repair mechanisms whatsoever
options.D: The amniotic fluid accelerates the speed of gamma photons

explanation: Tissues with high rates of cell division sustain much more permanent disruption from ionizing radiation, placing a pregnancy at high risk. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T5#BMP112_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is the main way gamma rays cause damage to living cells?

options.A: By raising the overall body temperature until proteins melt
options.B: By ionizing atoms and breaking molecular bonds like DNA
options.C: By draining all the water content out of the cell membrane
options.D: By blocking oxygen from binding to hemoglobin molecules

explanation: The intense energy of gamma photons strips electrons from atoms, creating chemical instability that directly damages vital genetic material. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T5#BMP112_U6_T5_h4)

question: Which medical device uses focused gamma rays to treat brain tumors without open surgery?
explanation: The Gamma Knife focuses many low-intensity gamma beams from different angles onto a precise point to destroy tumor cells without traditional surgery. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T5#BMP112_U6_T5_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of using radioactive tracers in diagnostic imaging?

options.A: To freeze blood flow so doctors can take clear pictures
options.B: To physically burn away diseased tissue from inside the organ
options.C: To emit gamma rays that external cameras map to view organ function
options.D: To provide nutritional energy to failing cells in the body

explanation: Tracers emit safe levels of gamma rays from inside the body, allowing specialized cameras to detect blood flow and metabolic activity. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T5#BMP112_U6_T5_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three core principles of radiation safety?
explanation: The standard radiation protection rules are time, distance, and shielding. Moving faster does not reduce radiation exposure doses. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T5#BMP112_U6_T5_h6)

question: Why do healthcare workers wear personal dosimeter badges in units with radiation sources?

options.A: To prove to patients that the equipment has been turned off
options.B: To track their cumulative radiation exposure over a working period
options.C: To block incoming gamma rays from striking their chest area
options.D: To sound an alarm when a radioactive patient enters the room

explanation: Dosimeters measure the total amount of radiation a worker absorbs over time, ensuring safety limits are never exceeded. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T5#BMP112_U6_T5_h6)
